T1.implementation_approach: Design a user-friendly interface using wireframes and mockups. Implement using frontend frameworks.
T1.notes: Focus on intuitive navigation and responsive design.

T2.implementation_approach: Develop RESTful APIs for problem repository operations like create, read, update, delete.
T2.notes: Ensure proper error handling and validation.

T3.implementation_approach: Design schema for storing problem details including metadata, constraints, and examples.
T3.notes: Optimize for query performance and scalability.

T4.implementation_approach: Create a UI for users to submit code with syntax highlighting and file upload options.
T4.notes: Include real-time feedback for syntax errors.

T5.implementation_approach: Implement a system to compile and execute code submissions securely in isolated environments.
T5.notes: Ensure sandboxing to prevent malicious code execution.

T6.implementation_approach: Design a UI for user profiles displaying achievements, statistics, and settings.

T7.implementation_approach: Develop APIs for user profile management including update and retrieval operations.

T8.implementation_approach: Design schema for storing user data including credentials, preferences, and activity logs.
T8.notes: Ensure data security and encryption for sensitive information.

T9.implementation_approach: Develop a UI to display leaderboard rankings with filters and sorting options.
T9.notes: Optimize for real-time updates and scalability.

T10.implementation_approach: Implement backend logic to calculate and update leaderboard rankings based on user activity.
T10.notes: Ensure efficient ranking algorithms for large datasets.

T11.implementation_approach: Design a UI for hints and tutorials with multimedia support and interactive elements.
T11.notes: Focus on engaging and educational content delivery.

T12.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to manage hints and tutorials including creation, retrieval, and updates.

T13.implementation_approach: Write unit and integration tests for problem repository functionality.
T13.notes: Focus on edge cases and performance testing.

T14.implementation_approach: Test code submission and evaluation system for correctness, security, and scalability.
T14.notes: Include stress testing for high submission volumes.

T15.implementation_approach: Test user profile functionalities including data retrieval, updates, and authentication.
T15.notes: Ensure compliance with data privacy regulations.

T16.implementation_approach: Test leaderboard UI and backend for accuracy and real-time updates.
T16.notes: Validate ranking algorithms and data consistency.

T17.implementation_approach: Test hints and tutorials UI and backend for content delivery and user engagement.

T18.implementation_approach: Deploy the platform using containerization and cloud services.
T18.notes: Ensure scalability, monitoring, and rollback mechanisms.

from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

# Initialize the SQLAlchemy object
_db = SQLAlchemy()

db = _db  # Direct SQLAlchemy instance

from app.database import db

class Problem(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'problems'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    difficulty = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp(), onupdate=db.func.current_timestamp())

    def __init__(self, title, description, difficulty):
        self.title = title
        self.description = description
        self.difficulty = difficulty

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<Problem {self.title}>'

from app.database import db

class User(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'users'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    username = db.Column(db.String(80), unique=True, nullable=False)
    email = db.Column(db.String(120), unique=True, nullable=False)
    password_hash = db.Column(db.String(128), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, server_default=db.func.now(), nullable=False)
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, server_default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now(), nullable=False)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<User {self.username}>"

    def save(self):
        """Save the user to the database."""
        db.session.add(self)
        db.session.commit()

    def delete(self):
        """Delete the user from the database."""
        db.session.delete(self)
        db.session.commit()

from app.database import db

class Solution(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'solutions'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    user_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('users.id'), nullable=False)
    problem_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('problems.id'), nullable=False)
    code = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    result = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    timestamp = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp())

    user = db.relationship('User', backref=db.backref('solutions', lazy=True))
    problem = db.relationship('Problem', backref=db.backref('solutions', lazy=True))

# app/routes.py
# Purpose: Aggregate all blueprints
# Layer: assembly

from app.controllers.problem_controller import problem_blueprint
from app.controllers.user_controller import user_blueprint
from app.controllers.solution_controller import solution_blueprint

# List of all blueprints to be registered in the application
blueprints = [
    problem_blueprint,
    user_blueprint,
    solution_blueprint
]

# Export the blueprints
__all__ = ['blueprints']

from flask import Flask
from app.routes import *

def create_app():
    app = Flask(__name__)

    # Register blueprints from routes or controllers
    app.register_blueprint(problem_blueprint)
    app.register_blueprint(user_blueprint)
    app.register_blueprint(solution_blueprint)

    # Additional setup can go here (e.g., configuration, middleware)

    return app

code_repository.readme_content:
# ACM Problem-Solving Platform

A website designed to help users solve ACM-style programming problems.

## Features

- Problem Repository: A comprehensive collection of ACM-style programming problems categorized by difficulty and topic.
- Code Submission and Evaluation: Allows users to submit code solutions and receive automated feedback on correctness and performance.
- User Profiles: Enables users to create profiles to track their progress, solved problems, and rankings.
- Leaderboard: Displays rankings of users based on their problem-solving performance.
- Hints and Tutorials: Provides hints and tutorials for selected problems to help users improve their skills.

## Setup

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python app.py
```

## Usage

Open http://localhost:5000 in your browser.
